title: Asia Helps Ralph Lauren Grow Faster

source.outlet: Ralph Lauren Corporation (press release filed with the SEC, Business Wire)
source.author: Ralph Lauren Corporation
source.title: Ralph Lauren Reports Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results Ahead of Expectations and Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
source.checked_against: Primary source (the company's own release as filed with the SEC). Web search on 2026-11-06 found no independent news coverage of the Q2 FY2027 results yet; search results only showed the same SEC filing (net income $297M, $4.87 EPS, $4.64 adjusted, inventory $1.2B down 9%), consistent with the release. No figure taken from any other source.

paragraphs: Ralph Lauren is an American company that sells clothes. Many people know it for its classic style, and some buy a whole outfit from the brand. On November 5, 2026, the company shared its results for the second quarter of its business year. The results were better than it had expected.
Revenue grew 9% to 2.2 billion dollars. When we leave out changes in the value of money between countries, revenue grew 10%.

The growth was not alike in every region. Asia was the remarkable one. Revenue there grew 28% to 571 million dollars. In China, it grew more than 35%. North America grew 6%, to 885 million dollars. Europe grew only 1%, to 696 million dollars, or 3% without changes in the value of money. So the regions did not look alike. Asia was not the sole region that grew, but it grew the fastest.

Prices also helped. In the company's own stores and on its websites, the average price of each item sold rose 9%. Strong sales at full price were one reason. In other words, the brand did not need big discounts to satisfy buyers. Many buyers still paid full price for a Ralph Lauren outfit.

Now look at profit. The gross margin was 74.2%. This is the part of each sale that is left after the company pays for the goods. However, this number needs care. Part of it came from a one-time refund. The company got back some of the tax it paid on goods brought into the United States. Without the refund, the gross margin was 70.5%. That was still 2.5 percentage points higher than a year earlier. The refund was not the sole reason for the higher margin.

The company also held less inventory. Inventory is the goods a company has but has not sold yet. At the end of the quarter, inventory was 1.2 billion dollars, 9% lower than a year before. Less inventory can mean fewer goods that later need big discounts.

The company raised its goals for the full year. Without changes in the value of money, it now expects revenue to grow about 6% to 7%. Before, it expected 5% to 6%. Patrice Louvet, the chief executive, said the strong quarter let the company raise its goals once again.

The prospect for the next three months is slower. This period includes the holiday season. The company expects revenue to grow about 3% to 4%, and it plans to spend more on marketing. That seems a realistic goal. The prospect of slower growth is also a realistic reason to plan with care.

These results highlight two points. First, Asia, and China in particular, now has real significance for the brand. Second, part of the high profit came from the one-time refund. That demonstrates the significance of looking at the numbers both with and without it. If the numbers without the refund keep growing, that should satisfy the company.
